[[Dayun Group#Motorcycles|Dayang Motors]] | website = [http://www.cpgroupglobal.com www.cpgroupglobal.com] | footnotes = | owner = [[Chearavanont family]] }} The '''Charoen Pokphand Group Company, Ltd.'''{{cite web|url=http://www.cpthailand.com|title=CP Worldwide|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060822041749/http://www.cpthailand.com/|archive-date=2006-08-22}} ({{Langx|th|เจริญโภคภัณฑ์}}; {{RTGS|''Charoen Phokkhaphan''}}; also commonly known as '''CP''') is a Thai conglomerate based in [[Bangkok]]. It is Thailand's largest private company and the largest privately held [[Royal Warrant of Appointment (Thailand)|Royal Warrant holder of the Thai Royal Family]]. The company describes itself as having eight business lines{{cite web |title=Business Lines |url=https://www.cpgroupglobal.com/biz-group |website=Charoen Pokphand Group |access-date=28 March 2020 |archive-date=23 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200723160327/https://www.cpgroupglobal.com/biz-group |url-status=dead }} covering 14 business groups. {{as of|2025}}, the group has investments in 21 countries.{{cite web |title=About CP |url=https://www.cpgroupglobal.com/en/about-cp/our-business |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200723163607/https://www.cpgroupglobal.com/about |archive-date=23 July 2020 |access-date=28 March 2020 |website=Charoen Pokphand Group}} It owns controlling stakes in [[Charoen Pokphand Foods]] (CPF),{{Cite web|url=https://www.marketresearchreports.com/blog/2019/08/27/world%E2%80%99s-top-10-animal-feed-companies|title=World's Top 10 Animal Feed Companies | Market Research Blog|date=August 27, 2019|website=Market Research Reports® Inc.}} the world's largest producer of feed, shrimp,{{Cite web|url=https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2019/09/17/cp-foods-building-land-based-shrimp-farm-in-florida/|title=CP Foods building land-based shrimp farm in Florida|website=Undercurrent News}} and a global top three producer of poultry,{{Cite web|url=https://www.wattagnet.com/articles/39203-asf-drives-poultry-outlook-for-2020?v=preview|title=ASF drives global poultry market in 2020|website=www.wattagnet.com|date=14 January 2020 }} pork, among other agricultural produces. It also operates Southeast Asia's largest retail business by revenue, with over 15,245{{cite web |url=https://today.line.me/th/v2/article/607JDN1 |title=LINE Today reports 15,245 participants in national initiative |website=LINE TODAY |language=th |access-date=7 June 2025}} [[7-Eleven]] stores the second largest in the world after the 20,000 stores in Japan{{Cite news|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/1914928/cp-bringing-7-eleven-to-cambodia|title=CP bringing 7-Eleven to Cambodia|last=|newspaper=Bangkok Post |date=8 May 2020 }} and a leading cash and carry business through CP Axtra, formerly known as Siam Makro.{{cite news|title= Now More than 10,000 7-Eleven Stores|url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/learning/advanced/1307966/now-more-than-10-000-7-eleven-stores-in-thailand|website=Bangkok Post|access-date=17 January 2018}} In the telecommunications sector, CP Group subsidiary, [[True Corporation]], is one of the largest telecom firms in Southeast Asia with over 48.8 million mobile customers.{{cite web |url=https://thereporter.asia/eng/2025/05/true-corporation-net-profit-q1-2025/ |title=True Corporation reports strong Q1 2025 net profit as customer base grows |website=The Reporter Asia |publisher=The Reporter Asia |date=May 2025 |access-date=7 June 2025}} With some 200 business subsidiaries in [[mainland China]], CP Group is known in China as "Zhèng Dà" (正大 - "positive" or "upright"). When China opened up its economy in 1978, the CP Group was the first foreign investor in the country and became the first foreign company registered in the special economic zone of [[Shenzhen]], Guangdong. The company is the single largest investor in mainland China today commanding over a fifth of China's entire feed meal market.{{Cite book |title=The Bamboo Network: How Expatriate Chinese Entrepreneurs Are Creating a New Economic Superpower in Asia |last1=Weidenbaum |first1=Murray L. |last2=Hughes |first2=Samuel |publisher=Free Press |year=1996 |isbn=978-0684822891 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/bamboonetworkhow00weid/page/32 32] |url=https://archive.org/details/bamboonetworkhow00weid/page/32 }} The corporate registration number was "0001." Through its extensive investments, CP Group has been credited with changing the country's dietary habits and leading China's green revolution. ==History== Charoen Pokphand traces its beginnings back to 1921. when immigrant brothers Chia Ek Chor ({{lang|zh|謝易初}}) and Mat U Ramus ({{lang|zh|謝進賢}}), hailing from [[Swatow]], China, started a seed store named Chia Tai Chung on Song Sawat Road in [[Bangkok's Chinatown]] during the reign of King [[Vajiravudh|Rama VI]]. They imported seeds and vegetables from China and exported pigs and eggs to Hong Kong, Taipei, Kuala Lumpur, and Singapore. The two brothers, who were virtually penniless, managed to scrape together enough capital to start their tiny seed shop. For the first few years of the businesses existence, the two brothers experimented to find their own market niche.{{Cite book |title=World On Fire |last=Chua |first=Amy |publisher=Knopf Doubleday Publishing |year=2003 |isbn=978-0385721868 |pages=41, 41| url=https://archive.org/details/worldonfirehowex00chua_0/page/41 }} By the 1950s, the shop began to specialize in exporting animal feed, particularly for chickens but the business struggled until the 1970s when the [[Bangkok Bank]] asked it to assume control of a bankrupt chicken farm. The shop later specialized in purchasing grown chickens for distribution to grocers and restaurants with vertically integrated strategy of feed-milling operations with chicken breeding. In 1969, the company had an annual turnover of US$1–2 million.{{Cite book |title=The Bamboo Network: How Expatriate Chinese Entrepreneurs Are Creating a New Economic Superpower in Asia |last1=Weidenbaum |first1=Murray L. |last2=Hughes |first2=Samuel |publisher=Free Press |year=1996 |isbn=9780684822891 |page=31 |url=https://archive.org/details/bamboonetworkhow00weid/page/31 }} When the Thai economy was liberalized in the 1970s, the CP Group entered various business negotiations with several major Thai banks, the Thai government, and foreign firms. The CP Group would supply Thai farmers with chicks and feed and teach breeders how to raise chickens while the farmers would sell the grown chickens back to the CP Group which processed the chickens and sold them to high volume grocery stores, restaurants, and fast food franchises across Thailand. The CP Group expanded internationally exporting their contract farming formula across Southeast Asia and around the world to Mexico, Taiwan, Portugal, mainland China, Indonesia, Turkey, and the United States. By the 1980s, with Thailand becoming a full blown capitalist economy, the CP Group entered the aquaculture business, turning their formula to raising and marketing shrimp. The company increased its scope from selling vegetable seeds under the trademark of Rua Bin ("Aeroplane") to production of animal feed under Ek Chor's two elder sons, Jaran Chiaravanont and Montri Jiaravanont. The company further integrated its business to include livestock farming, marketing, and distribution, under [[Dhanin Chearavanont]]. By the 1970s, the company had a virtual monopoly on the supply of chicken and eggs in Thailand.{{cite book | last=Phongpaichit | first=Phasuk | author2=Chris Baker | title=Thailands Boom and Bust | publisher=Silkworm Books | year=1998 | location=Thailand | isbn=974-7100-57-6 | url=https://archive.org/details/thailandsboombus00pasu }} The company was known for [[vertical integration]], expanding into several business lines, adding breeding farms, slaughterhouses, processed foods production, and, later, its own chain of restaurants. CP had also gone international, launching feed mill operations in Indonesia in 1972, exporting chickens to Japan in 1973, then moving into Singapore in 1976.{{cite web |url=http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/Charoen-Pokphand-Group-company-History.html |title=International Directory of Company Histories, Vol.62: Charoen Pokphand Group |website=Funding Universe|year=2004| access-date=2012-04-22}} In the 1980s, as mainland China opened up to foreign direct investment, the firm became the preferred partner for international brands such as [[Honda]], [[Walmart]], and [[Tesco]]. CP's family ties with the mainland enabled it to become the first foreign company to establish itself in the newly created [[Shenzhen]] [[Special Economic Zones of the People's Republic of China|Special Economic Zone]], where the company set up its Chia Tai Co. ({{lang-zh|s=正大集团|p=Zhèngdà Jítuán}}) subsidiary. In 1987, the company acquired the rights to the [[7-Eleven]] convenience store chain and the [[Kentucky Fried Chicken|KFC]] fast food restaurant chain. The company would also expand into Shanghai by manufacturing motorcycles under license from Honda and brewing beer with a license from [[Heineken]]. In 1989, CP entered the petrochemical business with [[Solvay (company)|Solvay]] of Belgium to launch Vinythai Co., a manufacturer of [[polyvinylchloride]].{{cite web|url=http://www.solvayplastics.com/sites/solvayplastics/EN/vinyls/Vinythai/Pages/CompanyProfile.aspx |title=Vinythai Company Profile |website=Solvay Plastics |date=2012-04-05| access-date=2012-04-22}} In 1990, the CP Group acquired a stake in [[TelecomAsia]], a joint venture with US telecommunications firm [[NYNEX]] to build and operate two million telephone lines in Bangkok worth some $3 billion. The CP Group also acquired interests in satellite launch, cable television, and mobile telephone services. By the early-1990s, CP presided over some 200 subsidiaries in China. CP's investment in poultry production on the mainland was credited with changing the country's dietary habits, as per capita consumption more than doubled by the end of the decade. Starting in 1993, many subsidiaries went public. TA, Charoen Pokphand Feedmill, Siam Makro, and Vinythai were listed publicly on the [[Stock Exchange of Thailand]] (SET); its Hong Kong subsidiary, CP Pokphand, on the [[Hong Kong Stock Exchange]]; a Shanghai-based animal feed and poultry group on the [[Shanghai Stock Exchange|Shanghai exchange]]; a real estate development arm, Hong Kong Fortune, on the Hong Kong Exchange; and Ek Chor China Motorcycle on the [[New York Stock Exchange]]. Having been listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange since 1981, CP Lotus, a retail arm of CP Group in China, opened its first store in Shanghai in 1997.{{Cite web|url=http://www.cplotuscorp.com/eng/about.php?page=milestone|title=Milestones {{!}} CP Lotus Corporate Website|website=CP Lotus|access-date=2017-02-24}} After the [[1997 Asian financial crisis|Asian financial crisis in 1997]], CP consolidated into three business lines under its main brands: foods (CP Foods), retail (7-Eleven), and telecommunications (True). By the early-2000s, the CP Group claimed $9 billion in business assets. The company sold its stakes in the [[Tesco Lotus]] venture with [[Tesco]] in 2003 due to its crisis policy in order to focus on [[7-Eleven]], in which, unlike Tesco, CP owns a majority, as its flagship retail arm. In 2013, Charoen Pokphand has got clearance to buy [[HSBC]]'s stake of Chinese [[Ping An Insurance]].{{Cite news| title= Thai tycoons go for it in multi-billion deals| work= Investvine| date= 2013-02-04| url= http://investvine.com/thai-tycoons-go-for-it/| access-date= 2013-03-17| archive-date= 2013-02-12| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130212084623/http://investvine.com/thai-tycoons-go-for-it/| url-status= dead}} On 10 May 2013, in spite of a lack of loan from the China Development Bank,{{cite web | url=http://www.morningwhistle.com/html/2013/FinanceMarkets_0108/216505.html | title=China Development Bank stops loan to Charoen Pokphand to buy Ping An | website=Morning Whistle | date=January 8, 2013 | access-date=2013-05-10 | author=Chen Xiaoyi}}{{cite news| url=https://www.scmp.com/business/article/1146336/still-too-much-murkiness-around-details-ping-deal | title=Still too much murkiness around the details of the Ping An deal | work=South China Morning Post | date=9 February 2013 | access-date=2013-05-10 | author=Yam, Shirley}} HSBC said "it was selling the 15.6 percent stake at HK$59 a share" to Charoen Pokphand Group.{{cite web | url=https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/1097953/ping-rises-hsbc-stake-sale-charoen-pokphand | title=Ping An rises on HSBC stake sale to Charoen Pokphand | website=Bloomberg Hong Kong | date=5 December 2012 | access-date=2013-05-10}} In 2014, CP announced a tie-up with the Japanese [[sogo shosha|general trading company]] [[Itochu]] under which CP acquired 4.9 percent of Itochu's listed stock for about US$1 billion, and Itochu in turn acquired a 25 percent stake in a Hong Kong-listed CP group company, CP Pokphand Co., for about $854 million. This transaction made CP the third-largest shareholder in Itochu, and was marketed as an alliance between the two conglomerates with a focus on developing international food trading opportunities.{{cite news|last1=Iwata|first1=Mari|title=Food Sets the Table for Asian Alliance|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/thailands-cp-group-to-buy-stake-in-japanese-trader-itochu-1406187364|access-date=5 June 2015|work=The Wall Street Journal|date=24 July 2014}} In 2015, CP and Itochu announced that they would jointly take a $10.4 billion stake in China's [[CITIC Limited]], forming a trilateral alliance with Itochu and CP each holding 10 percent of CITIC's stock, one of the largest foreign investments in a Chinese state-owned company.{{cite news|last1=Carew|first1=Rick|title=Itochu, CP in Deal to Take $10.4 Billion Stake in Citic|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/itochu-cp-take-10-4-billion-stake-in-citic-1421715748|access-date=5 June 2015|work=The Wall Street Journal|date=20 January 2015}} On 9 March 2020, CP Group submitted the winning bid to purchase Thai retailer, [[Tesco Lotus]], for about $10.6 billion.{{cite news |last1=Pananond |first1=Pavida |title=Tesco buyout gives CP undue power |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/opinion/opinion/1877839/tesco-buyout-gives-cp-undue-power |access-date=13 March 2020 |work=Bangkok Post |date=13 March 2020 |department=Opinion}} The purchase needed the approval of the [[Office of Trade Competition Commission]] (OTCC) as it could constitute a monopoly, given that CP already owns 7-Eleven convenience stores and the Makro cash-and-carry business.{{cite news |title=CP Group lands $10bn Tesco deal |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/1875239/cp-group-lands-10bn-tesco-deal |access-date=13 March 2020 |work=Bangkok Post |date=10 March 2020}} The sale became approved in Malaysia in November 2020 and in Thailand in December 2020, with rebranding of the acquired stores beginning in February 2021, replacing the Tesco corporate branding with that of Lotus's. In February 2021, CP Group was recognized as one of the World's Most Ethical Companies 2021 award from [[Ethisphere Institute]], a global institution for evaluating ethical business standards.{{Cite web|url=https://ethisphere.com/2021-wme-announcement/|title=Ethisphere Announces the 2021 World's Most Ethical Companies|date=23 February 2021}} In September 2021, CP Group raised $150 million from existing investors, raising the valuation of its Ascend Money subsidiary to $1.5 billion.{{Cite web|last=Burgos|first=Jonathan|title=Thailand's Ascend Money Backed By CP Group Reaches $1.5 Billion Valuation|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonathanburgos/2021/09/28/thailands-ascend-money-backed-by-cp-group-reaches-15-billion-valuation/|access-date=2021-10-12|website=Forbes|language=en}} In November 2021, CP Group and Telenor Group announced an agreement to form an equal partnership to support the merger of True Corporation and Total Access Communication (dtac). The aim was to create a new tech company that would contribute to Thailand’s strategy of becoming a regional technology hub, focusing on digital infrastructure and innovation.{{cite web |url=https://www.nationthailand.com/business/40009108 |title=CP, Telenor agree on merger to form new telecom-tech company |website=The Nation |publisher=The Nation Group |date=22 November 2021 |access-date=7 June 2025}} In 2023, Siam Makro Public Company Limited officially changed its name to CP Extra Public Company Limited (CPAXT). The rebranding was intended to clarify its business scope, which includes both wholesale and retail operations, and to support the company’s long-term growth under CP Group.{{cite web |url=https://moneyandbanking.co.th/2023/44264/ |title='สยามแม็คโคร' เปลี่ยนชื่อเป็น 'บริษัท ซีพี แอ็กซ์ตร้า จำกัด (มหาชน)' หรือ 'CPAXT' สร้างความชัดเจนธุรกิจครอบคลุมทั้งค้าส่งค้าปลีก |trans-title=MAKRO rebrands as CPAXT to align with CP Group’s long-term growth strategy |website=Money and Banking |publisher=Money and Banking Magazine |date=13 September 2023 |access-date=7 June 2025 |language=th}} ==Subsidiaries== ===Charoen Pokphand Foods=== {{Main|Charoen Pokphand Foods}} Known as Charoen Pokphand Foods Plc., (CPF). It was established in 1978 with operations in animal feed production, livestock breeding, further processing and trade. Currently, CPF invests overseas in nine countries, has subsidiaries in 17 countries {{Cite web|url=https://www.poultryworld.net/Meat/Articles/2020/5/CPF-Recovering-chicken-prices-record-profits-585894E/|title=CPF: Recovering chicken prices, record profits|website=PoultryWorld|date=21 May 2020}} and exports to over 40 countries. Furthermore, CPF is today the leading producer of feed and one of the largest producers of poultry in the world. Charoen Pokphand Foods is listed in the Stock Exchange of Thailand under the code: CPF. CPF reported sales revenue of approximately US$17.8 billion in 2024, with a market capitalization of over $5.9 billion that same year.{{Cite book |url=https://www.cpfworldwide.com/storage/annual_review/pdf_en_form4_EN_1743420229.pdf |title=Charoen Pokphand Foods Public Company Limited Annual Report 2024 |year=2025}} ===CP ALL=== {{Main|CP ALL}} '''CP ALL Public Company Limited''' is the flagship company of the Charoen Pokphand Group's marketing and distribution business. It has been the Thai licensee of [[7-Eleven]] since 1989 and operates 15,245 convenience stores under that trademark in Thailand. This is the third largest number of stores after the [[United States]] and [[Japan]].[http://www.cpall.co.th/ckfinder/userfiles/files/IR_data/AR-2016/CPALL_AR2016_Eng_280360.pdf CP All 2016 Annual Report] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170403114445/http://www.cpall.co.th/ckfinder/userfiles/files/IR_data/AR-2016/CPALL_AR2016_Eng_280360.pdf |date=2017-04-03 }}, CP All. Retrieved 2017-04-03. ===7-Eleven=== CP All Plc. is the sole operator of [[7-Eleven#Thailand|7-Eleven]] convenience stores in Thailand. The CP Group acquired the rights to distribute the convenience store in 1987. The first 7-Eleven outlet was opened in 1989 on Patpong Road in Bangkok. {{as of|2020}}, the company had a total of 11,700 stores nationwide employing 170,000 workers.{{cite news |last1=Kri-aksorn |first1=Thammachart |title=Here's why Twitter users boycott 7-eleven |url=https://prachatai.com/english/node/8399 |access-date=12 March 2020 |work=Prachatai English |date=12 March 2020}} Of the total, 4,245 stores are in Bangkok and vicinity (44 percent) and 5,297 stores are in provincial areas (56 percent). There are 4,205 corporate-owned stores (44 percent), 4,645 franchise stores (49 percent), and 692 sub-area license stores (seven percent). An average of 11.7 million customers visit 7-Eleven stores each day. In 2016, the company expanded another 710 new stores both as stand-alone stores and stores at PTT gas stations. At the end of 2014, the company had 8,210 stand-alone stores (86 percent) and 1,332 stores in [[PTT Public Company Limited|PTT]] gas stations (14 percent). The company planned to open approximately 700 new stores annually, with the goal of 10,000 stores in 2017.{{cite web|title=About CP All|url=https://www.cpall.co.th/Corporate/about-cp-all|website=CP All|access-date=16 May 2017|archive-date=3 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703041524/https://www.cpall.co.th/Corporate/about-cp-all|url-status=dead}} In 2024, there were 15,245 7-Eleven branches in Thailand, and in 2025, the company plans to invest in opening an additional 700 branches.{{cite web |url=https://today.line.me/th/v2/article/607JDN1 |title=CP All to invest THB 15 billion in 2025, adding 700 new 7-Eleven stores |website=LINE TODAY |publisher=LINE |language=th |date=6 June 2024 |access-date=7 June 2025}} === CP Axtra === CP Axtra Public Company Limited is a key retail and wholesale subsidiary of Charoen Pokphand Group, operating under the brands Makro and Lotus's. Established in 1988 as Siam Makro, the company opened its first store in Bangkok in 1989 and was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in 1994. In 2022, CP Axtra underwent a significant restructuring by amalgamating with Ek-Chai Distribution System Co., Ltd., the operator of Lotus's stores, consolidating its wholesale and retail operations under one entity. As of 2025, CP Axtra operates over 305 large-format stores across Thailand.{{Cite web |title=CP AXTRA PUBLIC COMPANY LIMITED {{!}} LinkedIn |url=https://th.linkedin.com/company/cp-axtra-public-company-limited |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=th.linkedin.com |language=en}} === True Corporation === {{Main|True Corporation}} The Telecommunications Business Group was established during the late 1980s. Known as True Corporation Plc, True offers a "convergence" of voice, video and data services across its integrated communications platform. Based in Bangkok, True currently services more than 23 million subscribers to its various services, which includes Thailand's third-largest mobile operator (TrueMove), the country's largest broadband and dial-up internet provider, largest fixed-line phone operator in Bangkok Metropolitan Area, electronic cash and payment services, personal communication telephone, data services, VoIP services, online portals, online games and is the only nationwide cable-TV provider (TrueVisions). True Corporation is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand under the code TRUE. True Corporation generated approximately US$3.1 billion in revenue in 2012, it had a market capitalization of about $4.3 billion in 2013. It is spinning off its infrastructure operations into a new telecommunications fund set to IPO at about $1.8 billion, putting the group's total value at about $5 billion.{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2013-12-05/true-infrastructure-fund-seeks-1-8-billion-from-thailand-ipo|title=True Infrastructure Fund Seeks $1.8 Billion From Thailand IPO|via=www.bloomberg.com|access-date=2013-11-07}} On November 22, 2021, [[Telenor]] and Charoen Pokphand Group, officially announced they have agreed to explore a US$8.6 billion merger plan between Thailand's second and third largest telecom operators (by subscribers), True Corporation (TRUE) and [[Total Access Communication]] (DTAC) – The proposed merger is subject to regulatory approvals.{{Cite news|url=https://www.yozzo.com/insights/a-deep-dive-into-the-true-dtac-merger-in-thailand/|title=A deep dive into the TRUE/DTAC merger in Thailand| work=Yozzo.com|access-date=2022-01-06}} The merger was "acknowledged" by the regulator NBTC at a meeting on October 20, 2022.[https://asia.nikkei.com/Business/Telecommunication/Thai-telecoms-regulator-allows-7.3bn-True-DTAC-merger Thai telecoms regulator allows $7.3bn True-DTAC merger] The newly merged company still retain the True Corporation name, which was founded on March 1, 2023, and it was listed on the [[Stock Exchange of Thailand]] under the stock ticker symbol TRUE on March 3, 2023.[https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/2481210/merged-true-dtac-to-be-called-true-corp Merged True-DTAC to be called True Corp] Q1/2025 True Corporation is one of the largest telecom firms in Southeast Asia with over 48.8 million mobile customers.{{cite web |url=https://thereporter.asia/eng/2025/05/true-corporation-net-profit-q1-2025/ |title=True Corporation reports strong Q1 2025 net profit as customer base grows |website=The Reporter Asia |publisher=The Reporter Asia |date=May 2025 |access-date=7 June 2025}} ===Ascend Group=== {{Main|Ascend Group}} Founded in 2014 as a spin-off of [[True Corporation]], Ascend Group handles the e-commerce, online retail, logistics and fulfillment component of CP Group. It marked its $150-million expansion by launching their affiliates in the Philippines and Indonesia, Vietnam, and also hard to reach economies like Myanmar and Cambodia. Ventures are classified under major subsidiaries: Ascend Commerce, Ascend Money and Ascend Capital, along with smaller independent ventures like TrueIDC and Egg Digital.{{Cite web|url=https://e27.co/startups/ascend-group|title=Ascend Group | e27|website=e27.co}} ===Lotus Supercenter=== '''CP Lotus Corporation''' is a retail operation in China.{{cite web|url=http://www.cplotuscorp.com/eng/about.php|title=Our Company - CP Lotus Corporate Website|website=www.cplotuscorp.com}} ===C.P. Pokphand Co., Ltd.=== Listed in Hong Kong, CPP is one of the world's largest producers of feed and one of China's leading agricultural companies with factories nationwide.{{cite web|title=Company Overview|url=http://www.cpp.hk/en/home/main.do?method=home|website=CP Pokphand Co., Ltd.|access-date=24 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160612063352/http://www.cpp.hk/en/home/main.do?method=home|archive-date=12 June 2016|url-status=dead}} ===CP Fresh Mart=== A Thai-based chain selling frozen foods and finished products, now with over 700 branches.{{cite web|title=Agro-Industry & Food|url=http://www.cpthailand.com/en/our_business/agro_industry_and_food.aspx|website=Charoen Pokphand Group|access-date=24 May 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150725043226/http://www.cpthailand.com/en/our_business/agro_industry_and_food.aspx|archive-date=25 July 2015}} ===Dayang Motors=== One of China's leading motorcycle producers [[Dayun Group|Dayang Motors]], recently signed a joint venture to begin production of cars in Thailand. Its motorcycles are exported to Southeast Asia, Europe, and Africa.{{cite web|title=Automotive|url=http://www.cpthailand.com/en/our_business/automotive.aspx|website=Charoen Pokphand Group|access-date=24 May 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428025855/http://www.cpthailand.com/en/our_business/automotive.aspx|archive-date=28 April 2016}} ===Solvay=== In 1989, CP entered the petrochemical business through a joint venture with [[Solvay S.A.|Solvay]], one of Belgium's largest chemical firms. But, it later sold its stakes. ===Wal-Mart=== In 1994, CP signed a joint venture agreement with American retail giant, [[Wal-Mart]] to establish super-retail stores throughout Asia and later dissolved it. ===CP Beverages & Food=== CP B&F is the Beverages arm of CP and was established in 2016 in Bangkok, Thailand. It operates Cafes, QSR, Logistics Brands namely Arabitia Cafe, Jungle Cafe, Farmee, Daily Runner and also is into Export - Import Business. The company now operates in 5 countries - China, Thailand, India, Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar and has 5 subsidiaries - CP B&F India Pvt Ltd, CP B&F (Thailand) Co. Ltd, CP B&F (Cambodia) Co., Ltd. In September 2020, CP B&F (Vietnam) Private Company Limited has been established in [[Vietnam]].{{Cite web |title=CP Beverages & Food (subsidiary company of Charoen Pokphand Group) {{!}} LinkedIn |url=https://in.linkedin.com/company/cp-b-f-india-private-limited |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=in.linkedin.com |language=en}} === SAIC Motor-CP === '''SAIC Motor-CP Co., Ltd.''' is a 50-50 joint venture between CP and Chinese automotive manufacturer [[SAIC Motor]]. It produces [[MG Motor|MG]] vehicles in a manufacturing plant in [[Chonburi]].{{Cite web |title=SAIC Motor |url=https://www.saicmotor.com/english/latest_news/mg/50359.shtml |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=www.saicmotor.com}} MG vehicles are distributed in Thailand by MG Sales (Thailand) Co., Ltd.{{Cite web |title=SAIC Motor |url=https://www.saicmotor.com/english/latest_news/mg/51812.shtml |access-date=2022-05-03 |website=www.saicmotor.com}} === CP Future City Development Corporation Limited (CPFC) === CP Future City Development Corporation Limited (CPFC) is a fully-integrated real estate company, a subsidiary of C.P. Group, established in 2021 to develop Makkasan then expanded to handle other projects claiming $14 USD billion in deveolopment assets and currently managing 800,000sqm of space, CPFC core businesses focus on property development, investment and management.{{Cite web |title=CP Future City Development Corporation {{!}} LinkedIn |url=https://th.linkedin.com/company/cpfuturecity |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=th.linkedin.com |language=en}} ==Shrimp feed supply chain traceability and audit== CP Foods produces and sells farmed shrimp. It does not own or operate any fishing vessels. The company has worked to improve the traceability of the fishmeal element of its supply chain since 2012, and broadened this effort to encompass a full traceability system for its farmed shrimp supply chain in 2014. As part of that process, CP Foods has reduced the number of suppliers who provide [[fishmeal]] for the production of shrimp feed.{{Cite news |last=Letters |date=2015-08-28 |title=CP Foods reasserts its strong commitment to human rights and a sustainable supply chain |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2015/aug/28/cp-foods-reasserts-its-strong-commitment-to-human-rights-and-a-sustainable-supply-chain |access-date=2026-03-03 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}{{Cite web |title=CP Foods joins forces with partners to shape sustainable seafood supply chain |url=https://www.cpfworldwide.com/en/media-center/1597 |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=www.cpfworldwide.com |language=en}} CP Foods has undertaken a full independent, third-party audit of its shrimp feed supply chain (all the way back to the individual fishing boats catching fish for fishmeal production), conducted by an international supply chain audit company. It's approved [[by-product]] fishmeal in shrimp feed is certified "IFFO RS CoC".{{cite web|title=IFFO RS History|url=http://www.iffo.net/iffo-rs-history|website=IFFO|access-date=6 June 2016|archive-date=25 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825224844/http://www.iffo.net/iffo-rs-history|url-status=dead}} ===Shrimp Sustainable Supply Chain Task Force=== CP Foods is a founding member of the Shrimp Sustainable Supply Chain Task Force (SSSC), established in July 2014, which has convened food producers, international retailers, and NGOs to map out a holistic improvement and audit plan for the Thai shrimp industry, and to identify and agree the steps and timetable to increase the sustainability and transparency of the supply chain.{{cite web|title=Shrimp Sustainable Supply Chain Task Force; Overview and Progress Update, May 2015|url=https://js.undercurrentnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/05/SSSC-Task-Force_Overview-and-Progress_May-2015_Short_Master_180515-11.pdf|website=Undercurrent News|access-date=6 June 2016}} The key aim of CP Foods and the SSSC is to ensure that abuse of workers and damage to the maritime ecosystem in the [[Gulf of Thailand]] and [[Andaman Sea]] is a thing of the past, and to restore trust in the industry. A U.S. court dismissed the lawsuit against Costco and CP Foods over allegations of selling Thai prawns linked to forced labor. The court ruled that the plaintiffs failed to prove the companies had a legal duty to disclose labor conditions in their supply chains and could not directly link the prawns they purchased to sources using illegal labor. CP Foods stated that it does not support forced labor and does not own the fishing vessels referenced in the allegations.{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/retail-giant-costco-wins-dismissal-of-prawn-lawsuit-over-thai-forced-labor-idUSKBN1592J8/ |title=Retail giant Costco wins dismissal of prawn lawsuit over Thai forced labor |website=Reuters |publisher=Reuters |date=11 January 2017 |access-date=7 June 2025}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * [https://web.archive.org/web/20160608062336/http://www.cpgroupglobal.com/en/ Corporate website] * [http://www.fundinguniverse.com/company-histories/Charoen-Pokphand-Group-company-History.html International Directory of Company Histories, Vol.62: Charoen Pokphand Group], St. James Press, 2004 {{Charoen Pokphand}} [[Category:Charoen Pokphand| ]] [[Category:Agriculture companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Conglomerate companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Real estate companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Retail companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Shipping companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Manufacturing companies based in Bangkok]] [[Category:1921 establishments in Siam]] [[Category:Conglomerate companies established in 1921]] [[Category:Food and drink companies established in 1921]] [[Category:Retail companies established in 1921]] [[Category:Telecommunications companies established in 1921]] [[Category:Siam companies established in 1921]] [[Category:Thai Royal Warrant holders]] [[Category:Meat packers]] [[Category:Companies in the IDX 30]] [[Category:Companies based in Bangkok]] [[Category:Privately held companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Holding companies of Thailand]] [[Category:Multinational companies headquartered in Thailand]]

The Charoen Pokphand Group Company, Ltd. (Thai: เจริญโภคภัณฑ์; RTGS: Charoen Phokkhaphan; also commonly known as CP) is a Thai conglomerate based in Bangkok. It is Thailand's largest private company and the largest privately held Royal Warrant holder of the Thai Royal Family. The company describes itself as having eight business lines covering 14 business groups. As of 2025, the group has investments in 21 countries.
It owns controlling stakes in Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF), the world's largest producer of feed, shrimp, and a global top three producer of poultry, pork, among other agricultural produces. It also operates Southeast Asia's largest retail business by revenue, with over 15,245 7-Eleven stores the second largest in the world after the 20,000 stores in Japan and a leading cash and carry business through CP Axtra, formerly known as Siam Makro. In the telecommunications sector, CP Group subsidiary, True Corporation, is one of the largest telecom firms in Southeast Asia with over 48.8 million mobile customers.
With some 200 business subsidiaries in mainland China, CP Group is known in China as "Zhèng Dà" (正大 - "positive" or "upright"). When China opened up its economy in 1978, the CP Group was the first foreign investor in the country and became the first foreign company registered in the special economic zone of Shenzhen, Guangdong. The company is the single largest investor in mainland China today commanding over a fifth of China's entire feed meal market. The corporate registration number was "0001." Through its extensive investments, CP Group has been credited with changing the country's dietary habits and leading China's green revolution.
